target_customer: Originally enterprises and consumers needing protection from facial recognition; later creators, marketers and developers buying AI talking-avatar video and APIs
problem: Faces in photos and video can be matched by facial recognition without consent. The founders later turned the same face technology toward generating realistic digital humans.
business_model: Initially privacy software; later SaaS subscriptions and usage-based API for AI avatar video
product_category: Face de-identification, then generative AI avatars and video

founders.name: Gil Perry
founders.background_notes: Named CEO and co-founder in the March 2022 funding release; background not found.

founders.name: Sella Blondheim
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page. Background not found.

founders.name: Eliran Kuta
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CTO on the YC page. Background not found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Adversarial manipulation of images to defeat face recognition, and later video reenactment, required deep learning research from a small team.

defensibility.rationale: The company describes patented video reenactment technology, but generative video models became widely available and rivals multiplied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought D-ID. By 2025 it acquired simpleshow itself, while competing with larger generative video players.

market_need_then: Fintech.global in January 2018 noted the seed came months before GDPR took effect in May 2018, which treats face images as sensitive data. Another source says awareness of facial recognition risks was low in 2017 and early VC interest was limited.

branding.name_origin: D-ID is short for de-identification, per several secondary sources

identity.voice_and_tone: Tech and creator oriented; branded the concept Creative Reality

branding.brand_signature: Creative Reality, the trademarked tagline, and the MyHeritage Deep Nostalgia feature powered by its technology
branding.community_and_virality: MyHeritage's Deep Nostalgia, licensed from D-ID, went viral in February 2021; one wiki-style source says it animated close to 100 million faces, which is approximate and unverified.

brand_strength.rationale: Exposure came mostly through partners such as MyHeritage rather than its own name, and the name reflects the original de-identification product.

pivots.from: Face de-identification to block facial recognition
pivots.to: AI video reenactment and digital humans (Creative Reality)
pivots.why: Sources describe the shift to AI video and avatars; the exact date and reason are not stated in opened sources, date approximate

outcome_analysis: D-ID started as a privacy tool for defeating face recognition and raised a $4M seed in January 2018. It then pivoted its face technology toward generating talking digital humans, gaining visibility through MyHeritage's Deep Nostalgia in 2021, and raised a $25M Series B in 2022 led by Macquarie Capital. Reported 2025 events include layoffs of about a quarter of staff and the purchase of simpleshow, so growth is real but the picture is mixed.
notes: Competitors left empty: the dated search found only NtechLab FindFace as context without a dated source. The Series A of $13.5M (2020, AXA lead) rests on aggregators (Seedtable, Simplify) and the AXA lead on one source. Totals conflict: release says $48M after Series B; $4M + $13.5M + $25M is $42.5M, so about $5.5M is unaccounted; TechCrunch 2025 says $60M to date. March 2025 layoffs of 22 staff come from a Calcalist listing in search results, not opened. The simpleshow acquisition is by D-ID, not of D-ID, so exit stays none. Jpost 2018 says founders served in a military setting with sensitive work, names not given.
